html:
Juan Santamaría was a Costa Rican drummer boy who died at the Second Battle of Rivas, in Nicaragua, on 11 April 1856, while setting fire to a building held by the soldiers of William Walker.

Walker, an American adventurer, had made himself master of Nicaragua and seemed to threaten all of Central America. President Juan Rafael Mora of Costa Rica raised an army and marched north. At Rivas the filibusters held a strong house, and Santamaría, by the story told later, carried a torch to it under fire and was shot.

He became the national hero, and the day of his death is a public holiday. The main airport of the country is named after him. The war against Walker united the states of the isthmus for a time, as Morazán had hoped.
sum: Juan Santamaría was a Costa Rican drummer boy who died at the Second Battle of Rivas, in Nicaragua, on 11 April 1856, while setting fire to a building held by the soldiers of William Walker.
